Subject: Re: ParcelPatch - sudden gen latency + throughput drop

Quick triage notes (on-call confirmed):
- No scheduled model rollouts at 08:50 in us-west-2 in the deployment ledger.
- Kernel scheduling observed elevated scheduling stalls on a subset of our pooled hosts (gpu-pool-az1) starting 08:47; correlate to a kernel preemption/recovery loop we saw in node logs.
- KV cache hit-rate for ParcelPatch tenant appears unchanged; batching profiles show a shift to smaller batch sizes (avg batch length down ~30%).

Hypothesis: a transient GPU scheduling regression caused effective concurrency to drop and led to shorter batches (lower batching efficiency) + higher tail latency.

Immediate mitigations we can do now:
1) Drain ~20% of traffic from the affected hosts and route to warm standby in us-west-2 (5–10m cutover).
2) Apply a conservative autoscale bump for ParcelPatch dedicated pool to increase headroom for 30m while we investigate.
3) Roll back any recent kernel/driver experiment if we find a correlate (investigation ongoing).

I'll start the routing drain now and post updates here. If we implement (1), we'll need a short note to ParcelPatch that we are routing to standby and expecting improved p95 within 10m.

Diego
SRE

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: ParcelPatch - post-incident summary and roadmap asks

Follow-up summary:
- Mitigation applied: traffic routing to warm standby reduced p95 to ~720ms within 9 minutes of intervention; throughput returned to within 95% of normal for ParcelPatch.
- Root cause (prelim): a GPU driver patch experiment in a private preprod cohort leaked into a small subset of production hosts via an automated rollout rule; the experiment caused intermittent kernel preemption loops on certain drivers and triggered scheduling stalls.
- Actions taken:
  * Immediate revert of the driver experiment (Diego)
  * Routing to warm standby while we validated stability (Hannah)
  * Drafted product asks and short-term guardrail proposal (Marissa)

Roadmap / action items:
- Marissa to create a scoped RFC for an autoscale safety floor for high-QPS tenants (owner: Marissa; due: 2026-11-19).
- Jonas to add a fast-variant-pin API to the serving control plane (owner: Jonas; prototype scope due: 2026-12-03).
- Diego to add a detection alert for kernel preemption patterns (owner: Diego; due: 2026-11-16).
- Avery to coordinate post-incident customer review with ParcelPatch next week (owner: Avery; schedule pending).

Attachments: parcelpatch-trace-1111.json (trace snippets), draft-customer-note-parcelpatch-1111.md (finalized short note).

Thanks everyone for the quick response. Please update the Jira INF-4217 with your timelines and keep this thread for any follow-ups with ParcelPatch.
